---
title: "Use the mesh in D-HYDRO"
---

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import netCDF4
from shapely import Point, box

from refined_quads import generate

workdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
quad_mesh = generate(
    box(155_000, 463_000, 155_320, 463_240),
    cell_size=32.0,
    refinement_areas=[(Point(155_160, 463_120).buffer(40), 1)],
    transition_rows=1,
    crs="EPSG:28992",
)
```

::: {.callout-warning title="Do not call it `mesh` next to D-HyDAMO"}
D-HyDAMO scripts usually import `from hydrolib.dhydamo.geometry import mesh` (the module
with `mesh2d_clip`, `links1d2d_add_links_1d_to_2d` and so on). `mesh = generate(...)`
replaces that module, and the next `mesh.<function>(...)` fails with an
`AttributeError`. Use another name, such as `quad_mesh` in the examples here.
:::

## Write a net file

```{python}
#| output: false
from refined_quads import write_ugrid

write_ugrid(quad_mesh, workdir / "mesh_net.nc")
```

The file is UGRID-1.0 with the structure of the D-HYDRO mesh generator export: the
`Mesh2d` topology with nodes, edges and faces, edge and face coordinates and face bounds.
For EPSG:28992 the CRS variable has exactly the attributes of the D-Flow FM plugin; for
another projected CRS they are derived with pyproj; a mesh without CRS gets no CRS
variable.

```{python}
#| echo: false
with netCDF4.Dataset(workdir / "mesh_net.nc") as ds:
    crs = ds["projected_coordinate_system"]
    print("variables:", ", ".join(ds.variables))
    print(f"CRS: {crs.getncattr('name')} (EPSG {crs.getncattr('epsg')})")
```

## Bed levels

The net file of `write_ugrid` has no bed level. Give it per cell after the mesh is in
the model, as `mesh2d_face_z` in the model's net file, with `bedLevType = 1`; no sample
file is needed. One rule makes this work in the D-HYDRO GUI as well
([ADR-0005](../adr/0005-bed-level-after-the-last-meshkernel-rebuild.qmd)):

> **The cells in the net file must be exactly the cells MeshKernel builds from its
> nodes and edges.** So: rebuild the cells with MeshKernel once more after the last
> change to the mesh, give the bed level to those cells, and change nothing afterwards.

The D-HYDRO GUI, like hydrolib's `mesh2d_from_netcdf`, does not take the cells from the
net file: it builds them again from the nodes and edges, and MeshKernel also makes a
cell of a small hole (a ring of at most six nodes). A bed level per cell only fits when
the file already holds those cells, in that order. Otherwise the GUI stops with "number
of values is not equal to multiple of all argument values" — or, with the same number
of cells in another order, puts the levels on the wrong cells.

::: {.callout-note title="What MeshKernel does with the cells"}
MeshKernel keeps nodes and edges, not cells, and finds the cells again each time it
builds them. Cells can **appear**: a small hole (a ring of at most six nodes) becomes a
cell, and a single cell a clip removed can come back. Cells can also **disappear**: a ring
MeshKernel does not take for a cell (more than six nodes) is no cell after the rebuild.
The model therefore holds the cells of the last rebuild, which can differ from the mesh
refined-quads made. `generate` and `refine` leave no holes themselves
([ADR-0004](../adr/0004-no-holes-meshkernel-closes.qmd)), but a clip in the model build
can.
:::

### With D-HyDAMO

```python
from pathlib import Path

import refined_quads
from hydrolib.dhydamo.geometry import mesh

quad_mesh = refined_quads.generate(
    domain,
    cell_size=32.0,
    refinement_areas=refinement_areas,
    transition_rows=1,
    water_areas=water_areas,
    crs="EPSG:28992",
)
net_file = Path(output_path) / "refined_quads_net.nc"
refined_quads.write_ugrid(quad_mesh, net_file)

network = fm.geometry.netfile.network
mesh.mesh2d_from_netcdf(network, net_file)  # MeshKernel builds the cells

# Other changes to the mesh (mesh2d_clip, branch clips, ...) go here, never later.

# The last MeshKernel rebuild: the cells as the D-HYDRO GUI will build them.
m2d = network._mesh2d
built = m2d.get_mesh2d()
m2d._set_mesh2d(node_x=built.node_x, node_y=built.node_y, edge_nodes=built.edge_nodes)

mesh.mesh2d_altitude_from_raster(network, rasterpath, "face", "mean", fill_option="nearest")
fm.geometry.bedlevtype = 1

# 1D2D links do not change the cells; then dimr.save(recurse=True)
```

Do not call the mesh `mesh`: that name is the D-HyDAMO module (see the warning at the
top). A clip after the last rebuild breaks the rule: on the Geul model a branch clip
removed one cell after the first rebuild, the hole it left became a cell again in a new
rebuild, and the net file had one cell fewer than the GUI would build. With the rebuild
after the clip the cell is simply there, as it is in the GUI.

`fill_option="nearest"` gives a cell without raster values the value of the nearest
cell; with `fill_value=-999` it would get -999 as its bed level.

**Check before opening the model.** Read the saved net file again as hydrolib and the
GUI do; the cells must be the same, in the same order:

```python
import netCDF4
import numpy as np
from hydrolib.core.dflowfm.net.models import Network
from hydrolib.core.dflowfm.net.reader import UgridReader

net = Path(output_path) / "dflowfm" / "network.nc"
with netCDF4.Dataset(net) as ds:
    face_x, face_y = ds["mesh2d_face_x"][:], ds["mesh2d_face_y"][:]
rebuilt = Network()
UgridReader(net).read_mesh2d(rebuilt._mesh2d)
assert len(rebuilt._mesh2d.mesh2d_face_x) == len(face_x), "MeshKernel builds other cells"
assert np.allclose(rebuilt._mesh2d.mesh2d_face_x, face_x), "cells in another order"
assert np.allclose(rebuilt._mesh2d.mesh2d_face_y, face_y), "cells in another order"
```

Tested on the Geul model (277,208 cells, D-HYDRO Suite 2026.02): the check passes, the
model loads in the GUI with the right bed levels, and D-Flow FM uses the level of every
cell exactly.

### Bed level on the nodes

To give the bed level on the nodes instead (`bedLevType` 3 to 6), sample the raster on
the nodes after the last MeshKernel rebuild; it is written as `mesh2d_node_z`:

```python
import types

# hydrolib fills NaN's (nodes on the edge, partly outside the raster) in place, but
# pandas 3 returns read-only arrays: let the raster statistics return writable copies
_stats = mesh.rasterstats.raster_stats_fine_cells
if not getattr(_stats, "_writable", False):
    def _writable_stats(*args, **kwargs):
        df = _stats(*args, **kwargs)
        return {c: types.SimpleNamespace(values=df[c].to_numpy(copy=True)) for c in df.columns}
    _writable_stats._writable = True
    mesh.rasterstats.raster_stats_fine_cells = _writable_stats

mesh.mesh2d_altitude_from_raster(network, rasterpath, "node", "mean", fill_option="nearest")
fm.geometry.bedlevtype = 3  # 3 mean, 4 minimum, 5 maximum of the node values
```

Tested with D-Flow FM 2026.02: every cell gets a bed level between the lowest and the
highest of its node values. Not yet tested in the D-HYDRO GUI.

### Which bedLevType

"Face" means two opposite things here. In the net file (UGRID 1.0) a face is a **cell**:
`mesh2d_face_z` is a level per cell. In the description of `bedLevType` in the MDU,
"at face" means at a **cell side** through which water flows (a flow link or u-point),
the finite-volume meaning. This table uses cell, cell side and node only.

| `bedLevType` | Input | Level of a cell side | Bed level of the cell |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | per cell: `mesh2d_face_z` | not measured (MDU: the higher of the two cells) | the cell's own value |
| 2 | per cell side: samples | the sample | not measured |
| 3 | per node: `mesh2d_node_z` | mean of its two nodes | the lowest of its cell sides |
| 4 | per node | the lower of its two nodes | the lowest of its cell sides, so its lowest node |
| 5 | per node | the higher of its two nodes | the lowest of its cell sides |
| 6 | per node | not measured | mean of its nodes |

Only cell sides shared with another cell count; sides on the edge of the mesh do not.
The cell formulas were measured with D-Flow FM 2026.02 on a mesh of 849 cells: each
matches the bed level D-Flow FM uses in every cell to 0.1 mm. In short: 1 gives each
cell exactly its own value; 6 the mean of its nodes; 4 its lowest node; with 3 and 5 one
low cell side makes the whole cell low.

::: {.callout-tip title="GeoTIFF fields in the D-HYDRO GUI"}
The GUI only reads rasters with the extension `.tif` (or `.asc`); with `.tiff` it stops
at "reading spatial operations". D-Flow FM and DIMR read both.
:::

## Read a net file

`read_ugrid` reads only the 2D mesh of a net file; a 1D network and other variables in it
are ignored. The lattice is derived from the square cells, so you can check or refine a
mesh from any program:

```{python}
from refined_quads import check, read_ugrid

quad_mesh = read_ugrid(workdir / "mesh_net.nc")
print(check(quad_mesh).summary())
```

## If the orthogonality repair does not close

D-Flow FM rejects a network whose edges are not orthogonal enough. The generator repairs
such edges; if that does not close, `generate` raises `OrthogonalityRepairError` with the
raw mesh (`exc.mesh`) and the problem locations (`exc.bad_points`), and the command line
writes `<output>_raw.nc` and `<output>_problems.gpkg` next to the output so you can look
at them in QGIS.
